info.title: Runware API - Kling VIDEO 4.0
info.summary: Unified video generation and editing with multi-keyframe control and clips up to 30 seconds
info.description: Kling VIDEO 4.0 is a unified video model that generates 1080p clips of up to 30 seconds from text, images, reference videos, and reusable elements. It follows up to 10 keyframes per clip, including first, middle, and last frames, and combines reference images, reference videos, and elements in a single request to hold subjects, style, and motion. It also edits an existing video from a prompt, which suits long narrative shots, storyboard-driven sequences, and reference-driven production work.

AuthenticationTask.title: Authentication
AuthenticationTask.description: Authenticates a connection using an API key. Can be sent as the first element of the request array as an alternative to using the Authorization header.

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task being performed.

connectionSessionUUID.title: Connection Session UUID
connectionSessionUUID.description: Optional session UUID to resume a previous connection and receive any buffered results.

model.title: Model
model.description:
Send `auto` instead of an AIR identifier to have the model router choose the model for this task. The rest of the request is unchanged, every value you send is kept, and only the parameters you leave out are filled in. See [Model Router](https://runware.ai/docs/models-api/model-router).

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/klingai-video-4-0#model)

referenceImages.title: Reference Images
referenceImages.description: List of reference images (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

items.title: Image
items.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

frameImages.title: Frame Images
frameImages.description:
An array of frame-specific image inputs to guide video generation. Each item can be either a plain image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64) or an object that pairs an image with a target position in the video.

The `frameImages` parameter allows you to constrain specific frames within the video sequence, ensuring that particular visual content appears at designated points. Position can be specified using `frame` (named positions or frame indices) or `timestamp` (seconds), depending on model support. This is different from `referenceImages`, which provide overall visual guidance without constraining specific timeline positions.

When the `frame` parameter is omitted, automatic distribution rules apply:

- **1 image**: Used as the first frame.
- **2 images**: First and last frames.
- **3+ images**: First and last frames, with intermediate images evenly spaced between.

**Examples**:

**Shorthand format:** When you don't need to specify a frame position, you can pass a plain image input directly.

```json
"frameImages": [
  "aac49721-1964-481a-ae78-8a4e29b91402"
]
```

**Object format:** When you need to specify a position, use an object with `image` and either `frame` or `timestamp` (model-dependent).

```json
"frameImages": [
  {
    "image": "aac49721-1964-481a-ae78-8a4e29b91402",
    "frame": "first"
  }
]
```

**First and last frames:** With two images, they automatically become the first and last frames of the video sequence. You can mix shorthand and object formats.

```json
"frameImages": [
  "aac49721-1964-481a-ae78-8a4e29b91402",
  {
    "image": "3ad204c3-a9de-4963-8a1a-c3911e3afafe",
    "frame": "last"
  }
]
```

**Multiple frames:** With three or more images, the first and last are anchored while intermediate frames are evenly distributed across the timeline.

```json
"frameImages": [
  {
    "image": "aac49721-1964-481a-ae78-8a4e29b91402",
    "frame": "first"
  },
  "c00abf5f-6cdb-4642-a01d-1bfff7bc3cf7",
  {
    "image": "3ad204c3-a9de-4963-8a1a-c3911e3afafe",
    "frame": "last"
  }
]
```

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/klingai-video-4-0#frameImages)

anyOf.title: Image
anyOf.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

image.title: Image
image.description: Image input (UUID, URL, Data URI, or Base64).

frame.title: Frame
frame.description: Target frame position for the image. Supports first and last frame.

video.title: Video
video.description: Video input (UUID or URL). Source video for prompt-based editing.

referenceVideos.title: Reference Videos
referenceVideos.description: List of reference videos (UUID or URL). Videos inside `elements` count toward the limit of 5 input videos and toward the combined duration limit.

elements.title: Elements

id.title: ID
id.description: Unique identifier for this element. Use to create a new element or reference a previously created one.

frontalImage.title: Frontal Image
frontalImage.description: Frontal reference image for the element. Required when using image-based elements.

images.title: Images
images.description: Reference images for the element. Up to 3 images. Requires frontalImage.

videos.title: Videos
videos.description: Reference video for the element. Cannot be combined with images or voices.

voices.title: Voices
voices.description: Voice audio for the element. Can only be combined with images, not videos.

positivePrompt.title: Positive Prompt
positivePrompt.description: Text prompt describing elements to include in the generated output. Images are referenced as `<<<image_1>>>` and videos as `<<<video_1>>>`. Images are numbered across `frameImages` then `referenceImages`, and videos across `video` then `referenceVideos`. Must satisfy `E / 26000 + N / 11000 <= 1`, where `N` counts the non-ASCII characters and `E` the rest.

width.title: Width
width.description: Width of the generated media in pixels.

height.title: Height
height.description: Height of the generated media in pixels.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Resolution preset for the output. When used with input media, automatically matches the aspect ratio from the input.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Length of the generated video in seconds. The total number of frames produced is determined by duration multiplied by the model's frame rate (fps).

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task being performed.

taskUUID.title: Task UUID
taskUUID.description: UUID v4 identifier for tracking tasks and matching async responses. Must be unique per task.

webhookURL.title: Webhook URL
webhookURL.description: Webhook URL that receives JSON responses via HTTP POST when generation tasks complete. For batch requests with multiple results, each completed item triggers a separate webhook call as it becomes available.

includeCost.title: Include Cost
includeCost.description: Include task cost in the response.

routing.title: Routing
routing.description: Model router options. Only read when `model` is `auto`, and never sent to the model.

preferences.title: Preferences
preferences.description: Relative importance of each dimension when models are compared. Weights, not thresholds.

quality.title: Weight
quality.description: Importance of one dimension. `0` leaves it out of the decision.

speed.title: Weight
speed.description: Importance of one dimension. `0` leaves it out of the decision.

cost.title: Weight
cost.description: Importance of one dimension. `0` leaves it out of the decision.

maxPrice.title: Max Price
maxPrice.description: Upper bound on what this request may cost, in USD. A model whose cost cannot be bounded is not chosen.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.description: Conditions the result has to meet, in plain words, such as a style or a feature. A model that cannot meet them is not chosen. Output size is set with width and height rather than described here.

numberResults.title: Number of Results
numberResults.description: Number of results to generate. Each result uses a different seed, producing variations of the same parameters.

uploadEndpoint.title: Upload Endpoint
uploadEndpoint.description:
Specifies a URL where the generated content will be automatically uploaded using the HTTP PUT method. The raw binary data of the media file is sent directly as the request body. For secure uploads to cloud storage, use presigned URLs that include temporary authentication credentials.

**Common use cases:**

- **Cloud storage**: Upload directly to S3 buckets, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage using presigned URLs.
- **CDN integration**: Upload to content delivery networks for immediate distribution.

```text
// S3 presigned URL for secure upload
https://your-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/generated/content.mp4?X-Amz-Signature=abc123&X-Amz-Expires=3600

// Google Cloud Storage presigned URL
https://storage.googleapis.com/your-bucket/content.jpg?X-Goog-Signature=xyz789

// Custom storage endpoint
https://storage.example.com/uploads/generated-image.jpg
```

The content data will be sent as the request body to the specified URL when generation is complete.

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/klingai-video-4-0#uploadEndpoint)

ttl.title: TTL
ttl.description: Time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for generated content. Only applies when `outputType` is `URL`.

outputFormat.title: Output Format
outputFormat.description:
Specifies the file format of the generated output. The available values depend on the task type and the specific model's capabilities.

- \`JPG\`: Best for photorealistic images with smaller file sizes (no transparency).
- \`PNG\`: Lossless compression, supports high quality and transparency (alpha channel).
- \`WEBP\`: Modern format providing superior compression and transparency support.
- \`MP4\`: Widely supported video container (H.264), recommended for general use.
- \`WEBM\`: Optimized for web delivery.
- \`MOV\`: QuickTime format, common in professional workflows (Apple ecosystem).
- \`GIF\`: Animated image format (no audio), suitable for short loops or previews.
- \`MP3\`: Compressed audio, smaller file size.
- \`WAV\`: Uncompressed, high-quality audio.
- \`FLAC\`: Lossless compression.
- \`OGG\`: Open-source compressed audio format (Vorbis codec).
- \`SVG\`: Scalable Vector Graphics.
- \`TIFF\`: High-quality output supporting layers.
- \`GLB\`: Binary glTF format for 3D models, including geometry, textures, and PBR materials.

> [!NOTE]
> \*\*Transparency\*\*: If you are using features like background removal or LayerDiffuse that require transparency, you must select a format that supports an alpha channel (e.g., \`PNG\`, \`WEBP\`, \`TIFF\`). \`JPG\` does not support transparency.

[Read full documentation](https://runware.ai/docs/models/klingai-video-4-0#outputFormat)

outputQuality.title: Output Quality
outputQuality.description: Compression quality of the output. Higher values preserve quality but increase file size.

deliveryMethod.title: Delivery Method
deliveryMethod.description: Determines how the API delivers task results.

oneOf.description: Returns an immediate acknowledgment with the task UUID. Poll for results using getResponse. Required for long-running tasks like video generation.

safety.title: Safety Settings
safety.description: Content safety checking configuration for video generation.

checkContent.title: Check Content
checkContent.description: Enable or disable content safety checking. Increases total generation time.

mode.title: Safety Mode
mode.description: Safety checking mode for video generation.

RequestBody.description: You must always POST an array of task objects.

taskType.title: Task Type
taskType.description: Identifier for the type of task this response belongs to.

taskUUID.title: Task UUID
taskUUID.description: UUID v4 identifier echoed from the original request, used to match async responses to their tasks.

cost.title: Cost
cost.description: Task cost in USD. Present when `includeCost` is set to `true` in the request.

videoDataURI.title: Video Data URI
videoDataURI.description: Data URI of the output video.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: The seed used for generation. If none was provided, shows the randomly generated seed.

NSFWContent.title: NSFW Content
NSFWContent.description: Flag indicating if NSFW content was detected.

ErrorResponse.title: Error Response
ErrorResponse.description: Standard error response returned by the Runware API.

code.description: A short identifier for the error (e.g., invalidApiKey, timeoutProvider).

message.description: A human-readable explanation of what went wrong.

parameter.description: The request parameter related to the error, if applicable.

taskType.description: The task type of the request that failed.

taskUUID.description: The unique identifier of the failed request.

400.description: Bad Request — Missing or invalid parameters.

401.description: Unauthorized — No valid API key provided.

403.description: Forbidden — The API key lacks permissions for this request.

429.description: Too Many Requests — Rate limit exceeded.

500.description: Server Error — Something went wrong on Runware's end.

503.description: Service Unavailable — Temporarily unavailable (maintenance or capacity).
